label: stereid band
parent: is_a portion of ground tissue (PO_0025059); part_of costa (PO_0030072)
definition: A portion of ground tissue that consists of a longitudinal strand of stereids (PO:0030045) in the costa of a non-vascular leaf, seen in cross-section as a band of thick-walled cells abaxial or adaxial to the guide cells.
reason: Standard character in moss floras (number and position of stereid bands in the costa). PO has the cell (stereid) and the costa but not the band. Propose to PO upstream (bryophyte anatomy).

In floras 'fibres' are mostly the fibrous remains of palm leaf sheaths (up to 80 cm long, black, robust), and sometimes mesocarp or bark fibres. PO plant fiber cell (PO_0025407) is a single sclerenchyma cell and does not fit. Without the organ it belongs to, the word is ambiguous.

Narrower: a dense, contracted, usually cymose cluster of flowers (Amaranthaceae, Urticaceae, etc.). PO lists 'glomerule' as a synonym of compound capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030122), but that is the Asteraceae sense and too narrow for flora usage, so do not use it here.

A lemmatisation fragment of 'axes'. Secondary or primary axes may be inflorescence branches or stem branches, so the word needs the organ it belongs to. The previous review rejected 'axis' for the same reason.
A length-to-width ratio ('3-7 × as long as wide'). This is pattern 11, ratio of two dimensions, of the part named in the sentence. It is not a bearer.
Narrower: a spike (Carex and other Cyperaceae) bearing only staminate flowers. It is both a staminate inflorescence and a spike inflorescence (PO_0030117). Counts go through pattern 03.
French 'pièces' means the members of any whorl (calyx, perianth, involucre, operculum). This is a generic part that needs the organ it belongs to.

label: asexual propagule
definition: A plant structure that becomes detached from the parent plant and grows into a new individual without sexual reproduction, such as a gemma, a brood body, a rhizoidal tuber or a deciduous branchlet.
reason: Used mainly in moss floras ('specialized asexual reproduction by...', filamentous propagules). PO lists 'propagule' as a synonym of fruit, which is wrong here. PO gemma (PO_0025614) is limited to structures on a thallus. Propose to PO upstream, with gemma and bulbil (FLOPO_0986055) as children.

label: perianth limb
parent: is_a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001); part_of fused perianth (PO_0025580)
definition: The expanded distal part of a fused perianth, above the perianth tube.
reason: The sibling classes perianth tube (FLOPO_0986010) and corolla limb (FLOPO_0986012) already exist. Floras with a fused perianth (Aristolochiaceae, Nyctaginaceae, Thymelaeaceae, Iridaceae) describe the limb's colour and width. Keep in FLOPO with the tube; propose to PO together with the corolla and perianth tube and limb classes.
Narrower: one tooth of a serrate margin, on leaves, leaflets, lobes or calyx lobes. The quality 'serrate' stays a quality of the margin. Use leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518) when the bearer is a leaf.
A generic surface feature (on seeds, pyrenes, fruits, stems) that needs the organ it belongs to, like 'pit' and 'groove' in the previous review.
Narrower: a rounded tooth of a crenate margin. The tooth shape is the quality 'crenate'. Use leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518) when the bearer is a leaf.

A dimension used as the second term of a ratio ('costa filling 1/2-2/3 of leaf width'). This is pattern 10, ratio to another part: costa width relative to the width of leaf PO_0025034 / non-vascular leaf PO_0025075.
A position adjective cut off from its noun ('3 pairs of distal leaflets'). It is a series position of the bearer (pattern 04), not a part.
A generic part (on a petal, corona or corolla throat) that needs the organ it belongs to. Where the statement only says the organ is pouched, use the quality saccate (FLOPO:0991140).
A generic outgrowth (of the calyx or another organ) that needs the organ it belongs to, like 'appendage' in the previous review.
A spikelet in the state 'fertile'. Fertile and sterile are listed context qualities of pattern 04. Counts go through pattern 03.

Narrower: the persistent, often woody base of a perennial herb (caudex or rootstock). The previous review mapped caudex to stem and rootstock to rhizome (a kind of stem). Stem covers both meanings; use rhizome (PO_0004542) when the text says 'root-stock'.
Exact: 'male inflorescence' is a RELATED synonym of staminate inflorescence in PO.

label: endocarp condyle
parent: is_a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001); part_of endocarp (PO_0009086)
definition: An intrusion of the endocarp into the locule of the fruit, around which the seed is curved, often hollow or perforate.
reason: The key character of Menispermaceae fruits (present or absent, perforate, globose), used in five floras. Keep in FLOPO; it is family-specific, so it is a low priority for PO.
Exact: the plural of an existing FLOPO class.

Narrower: a stalk-like base below the flower (for example the narrowed base of the hypanthium) that looks like a pedicel but is not one. PO stalk is the nearest correct class; flower pedicel would be wrong.
Narrower: a sterile bract on the peduncle, below the flowers.
Narrower: a compound, usually cymose inflorescence that looks like a panicle. It must not go to panicle inflorescence (PO_0030123), which is racemose.
An adverb fragment of 'deeply lobed / dissected'. It belongs to the quality of the following noun.

The end cell of a hair, filament, paraphysis or algal branchlet. It is a generic cell that needs the structure it ends. The previous review rejected 'cell'. Axillary hair terminal cell (PO_0025317) applies only when the text names an axillary hair.

Region of an existing class: the cells of the leaf margin, nearly always in moss leaves (papillose, linear, undifferentiated, forming a border). Use the bearer whose margin is meant, for example the margin of non-vascular leaf PO_0025075.
A network of veins on leaves, of ridges on seeds or pollen, or of fibres. It is ambiguous without the organ. Where the organ is given, the quality is reticulate (FLOPO:0991100).
A quality adjective ('3-tufted', 'tufted domatia'), or 'tuft' meaning a tuft of hairs, which is already covered by coma (PO_0020061) or bearded (FLOPO:0991118). It is not a part.
